issues.description: `rise_deadline_1p64_is_false_from_valid_low` (lines 187-197, listed as a headline theorem) can be proved without exhibiting any run of the circuit. Its only condition on the start is `v 0 ≤ 0.25`; it has no `-0.10 ≤ v 0`. `IsTrajectory` constrains nothing while the node is outside [-0.10, 2.08] V, so the constant -1 V function satisfies the exact statement, and the same form 'proves' that the output is never valid-high. The statement therefore does not establish what its name, its doc comment ('A 1.64 ns rise deadline is false even from a valid-low output') and the module docstring (lines 44-47) say. Two prose consequences in lines 44-47: '(at 0.25 V)' is true of the proof's witness but is not in the statement; and 'for a valid-low start the bracket is 1.64 ns to 2.34 ns' is not the bracket for the class the statement names, because the file's own run from -0.10 V is also a valid-low start and refutes 2.16 ns. The statement is verbatim from review/D05 (and P03), so the defect is inherited from the probe; matching the probe is not enough here. Fix: state `v 0 = 0.25` (it follows from `slow_rise_run 0.25`, and the trivial witness is then excluded) and write 'for a start at 0.25 V' in the bullet. Every other existential refutation in the four files pins the start in the safe domain (checked by listing them).

issues.description: The 'input slew bound' of IsTrajectory.of_feedthrough and IsTrajectory.of_charge_balance is a bound on the RIGHT DERIVATIVE of the input, and that is not a slew bound for an input with jumps. The ideal full-swing edge that takes its new value at the jump instant (the input class of the library's own exists_trajectory_step) has right derivative 0 at every instant, so every hypothesis of of_charge_balance is met with Su = 0 for every gate-drain capacitance CM in [0, 10] fF, the lemma returns a trajectory, and the 'node charge' of that v jumps by CM * 1.8 fC at the edge. So hq does not express conservation of charge across an input jump, and hSu does not exclude an infinitely fast edge; what excludes the physical (discontinuous) response is hcont on v, which the doc comments do not say. The doc comments state more than the hypotheses give: of_feedthrough 'where an input slew bound is needed', 'If the slews are bounded, |du| <= Su'; module header 'Su and Sg bound the slew of the input and of the aggressor'; of_charge_balance 'from conservation of charge'.
